answers.question: What do the last 5 sprints tell us for the next planning?
answers.message:
Sprint 25's **52 planned points is above anything the team finished in the last 5 sprints**, whose finished points ranged from 24 to 47 with a usual 31.
Likely · Board + Jira: The board and Jira agree.
Next step: Ask the team and product owner to cut Sprint 25 to about 31 to 40 points, starting with an 8-point story such as SHOP-260, SHOP-262 or SHOP-264. Check: Sprint 25 planned points at or below 40, and SHOP-269 and SHOP-270 estimated before the sprint starts.
Does SHOP-231, now in its third sprint, carry into Sprint 25? If so, it takes 8 more points from this plan.

Why:
- Finished points over Sprints 19 to 23 were 24, 47, 29, 39 and 31. Sprint 25 holds 52 points, 5 above the best sprint and 21 above the usual. (Board)
- Work was added after the start in 4 of 5 sprints: 1, 2, 0, 3 and 2 items. Sprint 24 has already added 3, so the plan has no room for them. (Board)
- Sprints 19, 22 and 23 each carried one item over, and Sprints 20 and 21 carried none. Most of the plan finishes, but a plan this size makes the carry-over bigger. (Board)
- Ruled out: Not scope taken out: removed and back to backlog are 0 in all five sprints. Misses came from unfinished work, not from cuts. (Board)
- SHOP-269, SHOP-270: SHOP-269 and SHOP-270 are unassigned bugs created 5 days ago with no estimate, so the real total is above 52. (Jira)

Options:
A. Cut the plan to about 31 to 40 points by moving out one or two 8-point stories Less committed scope, so the product owner has to reorder priorities Check: Sprint 25 starts at 40 points or fewer. At least 90% of planned items are finished at its end, as in the last 5 sprints (46 of 49). (recommended)
B. Estimate SHOP-269 and SHOP-270 before planning and hold a visible buffer for work added mid-sprint A few minutes of refinement, and a smaller committed plan Check: Both bugs have estimates before day 1. Added items in Sprint 25 stay at 2 or fewer. (recommended)
C. Keep 52 points but mark the lowest-priority items as stretch The stretch items are likely to carry over, and the team has to agree they are not a commitment Check: Carried-over items in Sprint 25 stay at 1 or fewer, with only stretch items among them.
Recommended because A cut brings the plan inside what the team has finished before, and estimating the two bugs shows what is really in it.

- SHOP-260, SHOP-262, SHOP-264: Three 8-point items, 24 points together. Leave out, or split one: what is the smallest slice that ships on its own?
- SHOP-263: 5 points, no dependency found. Make it optional: start it only when the committed items are done.
- SHOP-269, SHOP-270: Two bugs with no estimate. What size are they? Keep them in once sized, since they can hurt shoppers now.
- SHOP-261, SHOP-265, SHOP-266, SHOP-267, SHOP-268: Five small items, 23 points. Commit to these. Who takes each one?

Recommended because it fits the usual 31 points, leaves room for the bugs and for Sprint 24 carry-over, and uses small items that finish about twice as fast.

Does the team accept merging the 3-D Secure code behind the rollout switch before the provider's sandbox can verify it?

Why:

Recommended because the code is done and unreviewed, so review and a smaller finish line cost little and stop another rollover.
